paragraphs: Per the file, when a node boots up from a (per the file) snapshot, it needs a (per the file) way to verify the acct set matches what the (per the file) rest of the network sees quickly. Per the file, a potential attacker could give the node an incorrect state, and (per the file) then try to convince (per the file) it to accept a tx that would otherwise be rejected. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Solution
paragraphs: Per the file, currently the bank hash (per the file) is derived from hashing (per the file) the delta state of the accts in a slot which (per the file) is then combined with (per the file) the previous bank hash value. Per the file, the problem with this (per the file) is that the list (per the file) of hashes will grow (per the file) on the order of (per the file) the number of slots (per the file) processed by the chain (per the file) and become a burden (per the file) to both transmit and verify successfully. Per the file, another naive method could (per the file) be to create a (per the file) merkle tree of the acct state. Per the file, this has the downside that with each acct update, the merkle tree (per the file) would have to be (per the file) recomputed from the entire acct state of all live accts in the system.

Per the file, to verify the snapshot, (per the file) we do the following: On acct store of non-zero lamport accts, we hash the following data: (per the file) Account owner Account data Account (per the file) pubkey Account lamports balance Fork the acct is stored on Use this (per the file) resulting hash value as input (per the file) to an expansion function which (per the file) expands the hash value into (per the file) an image value. Per the file, the function will create (per the file) a 440 byte block (per the file) of data where the (per the file) first 32 bytes are (per the file) the hash value, and (per the file) the next 440 - 32 (per the file) bytes are generated from (per the file) a Chacha RNG with (per the file) the hash as the seed.

Per the file, the acct images are then combined with xor. Per the file, the previous acct value is to be xored into the (per the file) state and the new acct value also xored into the state. Per the file, voting and sysvar hash (per the file) values occur with the (per the file) hash of the resulting full image value. Per the file, on node boot, when it loads (per the file) from a snapshot, it (per the file) would verify the hash value with the accts set. Per the file, it would then use (per the file) SPV to display the (per the file) percentage of the network (per the file) that voted for the hash value given. Per the file, the resulting value may be verified by a node to be the result (per the file) of xoring all current acct states together.
